title: Basement Declutter App: photo -> Kleinanzeigen search -> sell/give-away/throw-away decision
description:
WHY: Personal tool to clear out a basement. User photographs an item; the
app identifies it, checks what comparable items go for on Kleinanzeigen
(German classifieds; no official public API), and recommends one of three
actions with a suggested price where relevant: (a) sell for <price>,
(b) give away, (c) throw away.

RECOMMENDED STACK (for review, not final until T1 spike resolves the
Kleinanzeigen access question):
- Backend: Python + FastAPI. Chosen over Node because the scraping
  ecosystem (httpx, BeautifulSoup, Playwright) and typical vision-API
  client libraries are strongest in Python, and it keeps one language
  across identification, scraping, and pricing logic.
- Frontend: Mobile-first PWA (React + Vite or plain HTML/JS), camera
  capture via <input capture> / getUserMedia, installable on a phone
  home screen. No native app / app-store distribution for an MVP used
  by one person.
- Vision/item identification: a vision-capable LLM (e.g. Claude with
  image input) given the photo, returning structured JSON: name,
  category, brand guess, condition guess, search keywords.
- Kleinanzeigen data access: NO official public API exists (Kleinanzeigen
  shut down third-party API access years ago). Some access method
  (scraping via Playwright, or an existing unofficial wrapper) will be
  required. This carries real ToS / bot-protection / legal-gray-area
  risk that is NOT resolved here -- see T1.
- Pricing/decision engine: simple rule-based logic over scraped
  comparable listings (e.g. median of active comparable prices), with
  configurable thresholds separating sell / give-away / throw-away.
- Storage: SQLite via SQLAlchemy/SQLModel -- single-user, single-machine
  tool, no need for a server-grade DB.
- Hosting: local machine or a small self-hosted box (e.g. home server /
  Raspberry Pi); no auth, no multi-tenancy.
- No auto-posting to Kleinanzeigen in the MVP: the app proposes a price
  and drafts a listing, but the user posts it manually. Automating
  posting is a further ToS risk and is explicitly out of scope here.

FLAGGED ASSUMPTIONS / OPEN QUESTIONS (not silently resolved):
1. Kleinanzeigen access method and its legal/ToS risk -- addressed by T1;
   nothing that depends on Kleinanzeigen data starts until T1 lands.
2. Sell/give-away/throw-away price thresholds are placeholders (e.g.
   ">EUR10 => sell, EUR0-10 with no working condition => give away,
   otherwise => throw away") -- to be revisited once real comparable
   data is available; encoded as configurable values, not hardcoded
   business logic.
3. Single user, no auth -- acceptable for a personal tool; flagged in
   case scope grows to multi-user later.
4. Vision LLM choice assumed to be Claude's vision API; swappable.

DONE WHEN: a photo uploaded through the app produces a stored Item
record with an identified name/category, a set of comparable
Kleinanzeigen listings (or an explicit "no comparables found"), a
suggested price where applicable, and one of the three recommended
actions -- visible in a results UI, with items trackable in a basement
inventory list.

title: Kleinanzeigen search: retry with progressively looser query on zero results
description:
INPUT: backend/app/comparable_search.py (sandbox-yqf.7) and
backend/app/identification.py (sandbox-yqf.6).

CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.7 found that identification.py's vision
prompt (identification.py:92) asks the model for "2-5 short strings
suitable as search terms" -- i.e. ALTERNATIVE candidate queries a human
might try one at a time -- but comparable_search.py's _build_query
(:284-288) ANDs all of them into a single query string via
" ".join(item.search_keywords). Live, a query like "ikea
schreibtischlampe lampe schreibtisch" will very likely return zero real
comparables even when the item is genuinely resellable, which silently
biases the downstream decision engine (sandbox-yqf.8) toward
throw_away/give_away for items that would actually sell fine.

This is a quality/accuracy issue, not a correctness bug -- the current
zero-results path IS correctly implemented and tested (empty list,
status still advances to pending_decision). This bead is about making
zero real results less likely to be a false negative from over-narrow
querying.

ACTION: On a zero-results response from the first (fully-joined) query,
retry with a progressively looser query before giving up: e.g. drop the
last keyword and retry, then try only the first keyword alone, up to a
small bounded number of attempts (do not retry unboundedly -- respect
the existing rate-limiting/backoff already in comparable_search.py).
Stop retrying as soon as any attempt returns >=1 result.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Existing tests continue to pass unmodified in behavior for their
  cases (non-zero results on first try, hard failures, etc).
- New test: a fixture where the fully-joined query returns zero results
  but a looser query (e.g. first keyword alone) returns >=1 result --
  assert the service returns the non-empty result set, not an empty one.
- New test: a fixture where EVERY progressively looser query returns
  zero results -- assert the service still correctly returns an empty
  list (not an error) and Item.status still advances to pending_decision,
  same as today's zero-results behavior.
- The total number of live search calls attempted per item stays
  bounded (assert an exact upper-bound call count in the all-empty test
  case, so this can't silently become an unbounded retry loop).

title: Fix enum value storage and Numeric/float type mismatch in Item/ComparableListing models
description:
INPUT: backend/app/models.py and backend/app/db.py from sandbox-yqf.3.

CONTEXT: reviewer found two real (non-blocking-for-.3, but real) issues
via mutation testing:
1. Item.decision and Item.status are stored in SQLite as the Python
   enum MEMBER NAME (e.g. "SELL", "PENDING_IDENTIFICATION"), not the
   lowercase snake_case VALUE the bead spec calls for (e.g. "sell",
   "pending_identification"). Both forms currently work on write
   because of the str-mixin, but raw SQL/exports/future Alembic
   migrations will see the wrong casing, and sandbox-yqf.4's API
   responses will likely serialize the wrong-cased value unless this
   is fixed first.
2. Item.suggested_price and ComparableListing.price are Python-typed
   as `float` (`Mapped[float]`) but the underlying column is `Numeric`,
   so reads actually return `Decimal`, not `float`. This will cause
   JSON-serialization friction (FastAPI/Pydantic) the moment
   sandbox-yqf.4 or sandbox-yqf.9 return an Item in an API response.

ACTION:
1. Fix the enum columns to store `.value` (lowercase snake_case) instead
   of `.name`, e.g. via SQLAlchemy's `Enum(..., values_callable=lambda
   e: [m.value for m in e])`, or equivalent. Existing rows: no migration
   needed for existing data since this is pre-launch/no real data yet --
   just fix the mapping going forward.
2. Fix the price/suggested_price type mismatch: either (a) change the
   column type so it genuinely round-trips as `float`, or (b) keep
   `Numeric`/`Decimal` deliberately for money-precision reasons and fix
   the Python type hints to `Mapped[Decimal]` plus decide+document how
   API beads (.4, .9) should serialize it to JSON (e.g. cast to float at
   the API boundary, or serialize as string). Pick one approach and
   document the reasoning in the same docstring location sandbox-yqf.3
   used for the migration-mechanism choice.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Existing test suite (backend/tests/) still passes unmodified in
  behavior (only touching the two issues above).
- New test: after committing an Item with decision=Decision.sell,
  querying the raw stored value via sqlite3 (or engine.execute of raw
  SQL) confirms the stored value is "sell", not "SELL". Same pattern
  for one status value.
- New test: after committing an Item/ComparableListing with a price,
  reading it back and confirming the returned Python value matches
  whichever type was chosen in step 2 above (float if (a), Decimal if
  (b)) -- and if (b), a test demonstrating the documented
  JSON-serialization approach actually produces valid JSON (e.g. via
  Pydantic model_dump_json() or json.dumps with a custom encoder, not
  just asserting no exception).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently verified via raw sqlite3 read that decision/status now store lowercase .value ('sell', 'given_away'), verified DDL changed Numeric->Float and reads return real Python float (not Decimal), confirmed via baseline diff (40 vs 42) that the fix is purely additive with zero pre-existing assertions weakened, and confirmed enum member names/values themselves are unchanged (only DB column mapping changed). All 30 tests from sandbox-yqf.6/.7 still pass against the changed models -- no regression.

title: Pricing & sell/give-away/throw-away decision engine
description:
INPUT: an Item with its associated ComparableListing rows (from the
search module).

ACTION: Implement decision logic:
- Compute a suggested_price from comparable listings (e.g. median of
  active comparable prices; document the exact formula chosen).
- Classify into one of three decisions using configurable thresholds
  (not hardcoded magic numbers -- read from a config module/file):
  a) sell: median comparable price >= SELL_THRESHOLD (placeholder
     default e.g. EUR10, per epic assumption #2)
  b) give_away: below SELL_THRESHOLD but item condition is usable /
     comparables exist at low price
  c) throw_away: no comparables found AND/OR item condition indicates
     broken/unusable
- Update the Item row: suggested_price, decision, status=decided.

OUTPUT: decision engine + tests.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Unit test: comparables with median price above threshold ->
  decision=sell with correct suggested_price.
- Unit test: comparables present but below threshold, item usable ->
  decision=give_away.
- Unit test: zero comparables and/or condition=broken -> decision=
  throw_away.
- Thresholds are read from a single named config location, verified by
  a test that changing the config value changes the classification
  boundary.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently re-derived all done-criteria in a fresh test file (not reading the implementer's tests) -- median computation, threshold boundary inclusivity, monkeypatch-both-directions threshold test, condition=broken always winning over high comparables, and a real SQLite round-trip confirming no regression of the sandbox-yqf.14 enum fix. Zero-comparables->throw_away judgment call confirmed as a defensible reading of the bead text, documented in code not just chat. Fixed one cosmetic lint nit (unused import) myself. Pinned a real integration note into sandbox-yqf.9: decide_item doesn't check incoming status, so .9 must only call it once status has genuinely reached pending_decision.

title: Pipeline orchestration: photo -> decision end-to-end + GET /items/{id}
description:
INPUT: the upload endpoint, identification service, search module, and
decision engine, all already implemented.

ACTION: Wire the four steps into a single pipeline triggered after photo
upload (in-process sequential calls is sufficient for this scale; no
message queue needed): upload -> identify -> search -> decide, updating
Item.status at each stage. Add `GET /items/{id}` returning the full Item
record including its comparable listings, suggested price, decision, and
current status (so a client can poll while the pipeline runs, or fetch
after it's synchronously done -- pick synchronous execution within the
upload request unless that risks request timeouts, in which case run it
as a background task and document the polling contract).

EDGE CASES: if any pipeline stage fails (per that stage's documented
failure behavior), GET /items/{id} must still return a valid response
showing the stage the item is stuck at, not a 500.

OUTPUT: orchestration code + `GET /items/{id}` endpoint + tests.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Integration test: uploading a fixture photo (with identification and
  search mocked/stubbed) results in a fetchable Item via GET /items/{id}
  showing decision, suggested_price, and comparable listings populated
  end-to-end.
- Integration test covers a stage failure (e.g. mocked search failure)
  and asserts GET /items/{id} still returns 200 with a status reflecting
  where the pipeline stalled, not a crash.
notes:
Addendum from sandbox-yqf.6 review (identification service):
1. ItemIdentificationService.identify_item mutates the Item ORM object
   in place but deliberately does NOT commit a DB session -- this
   task (.9, pipeline orchestration) owns the session and must commit
   after calling it, or the identification results won't persist.
2. identify_item returns a bool indicating success/failure. .9 must
   check this return value -- on False (API failure), leave the
   pipeline at status=pending_identification for retry rather than
   silently proceeding to the search step as if identification
   succeeded.
Addendum from sandbox-yqf.8 review (decision engine):
PricingDecisionService.decide_item does NOT check the incoming
Item.status before classifying -- it will happily classify an item
still stuck at pending_search (e.g. because sandbox-yqf.7's search
step failed/exhausted retries) as throw_away, since it just sees
"zero comparables" with no way to distinguish "genuinely searched,
found nothing" from "search never actually completed". This
orchestration task (.9) must guard the pipeline ordering itself: only
call decide_item once status has actually reached pending_decision
(i.e. the search step succeeded, even if it succeeded with zero
results) -- do not call it on an item still at pending_search.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: 68/68 tests pass, ran the pipeline test file 5x for flakiness (none found). Critical check -- ran a REAL uvicorn server (not just TestClient) with 10 concurrent uploads to verify the BackgroundTasks threading model doesn't break SQLite; zero threading/locking errors, confirmed check_same_thread=False from db.py plus a fresh per-thread session in run_pipeline_with_new_session makes this safe. Both mandatory integration requirements (commit+check identify_item's bool; only call decide_item once status reaches pending_decision) verified as real code at specific line numbers, not just test assertions. Ruff clean (implementer's 'no linter' claim was wrong -- ruff exists and reviewer ran it). Fixed a docstring typo myself.

title: Vision-based item identification service
description:
INPUT: an Item row with a stored photo (status=pending_identification).

ACTION: Implement a backend service that sends the item's photo to a
vision-capable LLM API and parses the response into structured fields:
name, category, brand (nullable), condition guess, search_keywords
(list of strings suitable for a Kleinanzeigen search query). Update the
Item row with these fields and advance status to pending_search.

Use Claude's vision API as the default provider (per epic's flagged
assumption #4), but isolate the call behind a small interface so the
provider can be swapped later.

EDGE CASES:
- API call failure/timeout: leave status as pending_identification, log
  the error, do not crash the pipeline -- surfaced as a retryable state.
- Ambiguous/unidentifiable photo: still return a best-effort name (e.g.
  "unidentified item") rather than leaving fields null, so downstream
  steps have something to search with.

OUTPUT: identification service + tests.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Unit test with a mocked LLM response validates correct parsing into
  Item fields for a well-formed response.
- Unit test covers the API-failure edge case: status remains
  pending_identification and no exception propagates uncaught.
- Unit test covers the ambiguous-photo edge case producing a
  non-null fallback name/keywords.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: mocked LLM response confirmed genuinely mocked (re-ran full suite with network calls monkey-patched to raise + no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, still 22 passed); failure and ambiguous-photo edge cases verified as real assertions, not comment-only conventions; provider abstraction and lazy client construction confirmed. Bumped default vision model from a prior-gen ID to claude-sonnet-5 (trivial one-line fix, orchestrator's own edit, re-ran suite after). Two non-blocking integration notes (service doesn't commit; caller must check bool return) pinned into sandbox-yqf.9's notes.

title: Kleinanzeigen comparable-listings search module
description:
INPUT: the access method decided in the Kleinanzeigen spike doc
(docs/kleinanzeigen-access.md), and the ComparableListing data model.

ACTION: Implement a search module that, given search keywords, returns a
list of comparable Kleinanzeigen listings (title, price, url, condition,
location) using exactly the method documented in the spike. Persist
results as ComparableListing rows linked to the Item, and advance status
to pending_decision.

EDGE CASES:
- Zero results found: return an empty list (not an error) -- this is a
  valid signal the decision engine (next task) needs to see, e.g. "no
  comparables found" -> likely throw_away or give_away.
- Network/scrape failure: retry once, then fail gracefully leaving
  status at pending_search with a logged error (not crash the pipeline).
- Rate limiting: implement whatever delay/backoff policy the spike doc
  specifies.

OUTPUT: search module + tests using recorded/fixture HTML or mocked
responses (no live scraping in automated tests, to keep tests
deterministic and avoid hammering the live site).

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Unit tests against fixture data return correctly parsed
  ComparableListing objects (title/price/url/condition/location all
  populated).
- Zero-results and failure edge cases each have a passing test matching
  the behavior above.
- A manual smoke-test procedure against the live site is documented in
  the task summary (not required to run in CI).
notes:
Addendum from sandbox-yqf.1 spike review (docs/kleinanzeigen-access.md),
two decisions this task must follow rather than leave open:

1. sort_type: use "DATE_DESCENDING" (newest first), NOT
   "PRICE_ASCENDING". Sorting comparables by price-ascending biases the
   median/suggested price low -- reviewer flagged this explicitly.

2. location/distance_km: pass an explicit nationwide-equivalent policy
   -- either leave location=None (searches all of Germany per the
   library's docs) or pick a documented default; do NOT let an
   unresolvable location string raise ValueError uncaught. Decide and
   document whichever default you use in this task's own output.

Also noted by the reviewer as a residual, non-blocking risk: the spike's
findings on Kleinanzeigen's actual robots.txt/ToS text could not be
verified from inside this sandbox (kleinanzeigen.de and adevinta.com are
blocked by sandbox egress policy) -- the doc is explicit that this is
inferred from secondhand sources, not a firsthand read. If this task's
execution environment has unrestricted egress, a quick robots.txt check
before implementing is cheap insurance, not required.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently confirmed 40/40 tests pass (re-ran with sockets monkey-patched to raise -- zero live network proven, not claimed), sort_type=DATE_DESCENDING and location=None both verified as hardcoded/enforced with real tests (incl. ValueError-wrapping for unresolvable locations), condition extraction from the library's localized attributes dict confirmed genuine (not stubbed), retry-once and zero-results edge cases both correctly implemented and tested, FK persistence verified via ad-hoc session. One real but non-blocking design concern (query-joining of alternative search terms likely yields spurious zero-results live) filed as sandbox-yqf.15.

title: Data model & migrations: Item + ComparableListing
description:
INPUT: the scaffolded backend from the scaffolding task.

ACTION: Define persistence layer using SQLAlchemy/SQLModel against
SQLite:
- `Item` table: id, photo_path, identified_name, category, brand,
  condition, search_keywords (list/JSON), suggested_price, decision
  (enum: pending | sell | give_away | throw_away), status (enum:
  pending_identification | pending_search | pending_decision |
  decided | listed | given_away | disposed), created_at, updated_at.
- `ComparableListing` table: id, item_id (FK), title, price, url,
  condition, location, fetched_at.
- Migration mechanism (Alembic, or simple create-all for this scale --
  pick one and document the choice).

OUTPUT: model files + migration, committed.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Unit tests create an Item, attach ComparableListing rows, and read
  them back correctly against a throwaway SQLite test DB.
- Enum fields reject invalid values (test asserts this).
- Migration/create-all runs cleanly against an empty DB file.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently re-ran tests (9 passed), reproduced create_all against a fresh DB, and mutation-tested the enum-rejection and FK-integrity tests (flipped enforcement off, confirmed they correctly fail) to verify they're not no-ops. search_keywords JSON round-trip verified via raw sqlite3 read. Scope clean: models/db/tests/requirements.txt only. Two non-blocking-for-this-bead but real downstream issues (enum stored as .name not .value; price/suggested_price typed float but returns Decimal) filed as sandbox-yqf.14 and gated in front of sandbox-yqf.4.

title: Backend: photo upload endpoint
description:
INPUT: the Item data model.

ACTION: Implement `POST /items` accepting a multipart image upload.
Store the image file on disk (e.g. `backend/uploads/<uuid>.<ext>`), create
an Item row with status=pending_identification and photo_path set, and
return the created item (id + status) as JSON.

EDGE CASES:
- Reject non-image content types with 400 and a clear error message.
- Reject uploads over a defined max size (e.g. 10MB) with 413.
- Handle missing/empty file part with 400.

OUTPUT: working endpoint + tests.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Integration test: uploading a valid fixture JPEG returns 201 with an
  item id, and the Item row exists in the DB with status
  pending_identification and a photo_path pointing to a real file.
- Tests cover the three edge cases above with correct status codes.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently probed the endpoint against a real uvicorn server (not just TestClient) -- confirmed both size-check layers work (chunked upload with no Content-Length header at all still caught by the authoritative byte-count at exactly/over the 10MB boundary), confirmed no leftover files/rows on any failure path, confirmed the .14 enum fix holds through this endpoint via raw SQL read, confirmed test isolation (uploads dir doesn't survive the suite). 51/51 tests pass. Scope clean.

title: Scaffold repo: FastAPI backend + PWA frontend skeleton
description:
INPUT: empty/near-empty repo.

ACTION: Create the base project structure:
- `backend/`: FastAPI app skeleton with a `GET /health` endpoint
  returning 200 + {"status": "ok"}.
- `frontend/`: minimal PWA skeleton (React+Vite, or plain HTML/JS/manifest
  if simpler) that can be served and shows a placeholder home page.
- `docker-compose.yml` at repo root that builds and runs both services
  together for local dev.
- Basic backend test setup (pytest) with one passing test hitting
  `/health`.
- README section documenting `docker compose up` and how to run backend
  tests.

OUTPUT: buildable/runnable skeleton, committed.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- `docker compose up` starts both services without error.
- `curl http://localhost:<port>/health` returns 200 with the expected
  JSON body.
- `pytest` (or equivalent) passes in the backend.
- Frontend placeholder page loads in a browser without console errors.

EDGE CASES: Do not wire any Kleinanzeigen, vision, or DB logic here --
scaffolding only. If Docker isn't available in the execution environment,
fall back to documenting equivalent `uvicorn`/`npm run dev` commands and
note the limitation in the summary.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: pytest passes, /health returns 200, frontend dev/build clean, docker compose config valid; docker compose up itself unverifiable in this sandbox due to egress proxy blocking Docker Hub's blob CDN (confirmed independently, not a misconfig). No scope creep into Kleinanzeigen/vision/DB.

title: Spike: determine Kleinanzeigen data-access method
description:
INPUT: none (research/investigation task).

ACTION: Investigate and decide how this app will query Kleinanzeigen for
comparable listings. Cover:
1. Confirm there is no official public search/listings API (Kleinanzeigen
   retired third-party API access) -- verify current state, don't assume
   stale.
2. Check Kleinanzeigen's robots.txt and Terms of Service for what
   automated access is/isn't permitted.
3. Survey existing open-source approaches (e.g. unofficial scraper
   libraries/wrappers on GitHub/PyPI) and evaluate maturity/maintenance.
4. Decide a concrete access method for T7 to implement (e.g. Playwright
   headless browser against search result pages, with rate limiting and
   a realistic user-agent/delay policy) OR flag that no viable method
   exists and this needs a design pivot (e.g. manual paste-in of
   comparable prices as a fallback).
5. Note the legal/ToS risk level explicitly (this is a personal-use tool,
   not a commercial product) rather than silently assuming it's fine.

OUTPUT: a markdown decision doc at `docs/kleinanzeigen-access.md`
committed to the repo, containing: findings for points 1-3, the chosen
method (or fallback) from point 4, and the risk note from point 5.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- `docs/kleinanzeigen-access.md` exists and explicitly answers all 5
  points above.
- The doc states one concrete, unambiguous method that T7 will
  implement against (not a list of options left open).
- No code implementation in this task -- documentation only.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS: independently re-verified sandbox egress blocks on kleinanzeigen.de/adevinta.com and GitHub scoping are real, package claims checked against PyPI's own JSON API, and a full honesty audit found no secondhand evidence stated as verified fact anywhere in the doc. Concrete, unambiguous method decided for sandbox-yqf.7. Minor residual gaps (sort_type bias, location policy) folded into sandbox-yqf.7's notes.

title: Upload endpoint: case-insensitive content-type check + reject SVG/sniff magic bytes
description: INPUT: backend/app/main.py POST /items (sandbox-yqf.4). CONTEXT: reviewer of sandbox-yqf.4 found two minor gaps in the non-image-rejection check at main.py:113: 1. The content-type comparison is case-sensitive, so a technically valid "IMAGE/JPEG" header (HTTP media types are case-insensitive per RFC 9110) would be wrongly rejected with 400. Unlikely from browsers but worth fixing for correctness. 2. image/svg+xml and image/heic are accepted with no magic-byte sniffing (only Content-Type header is checked). An SVG can contain embedded

title: docker-compose bind mounts miss frontend config files (index.html, vite.config.js, package.json)
description:
Found during review of sandbox-yqf.2. docker-compose.yml only bind-mounts
./frontend/src and ./frontend/public into the frontend container, so
editing frontend/index.html, frontend/vite.config.js, or
frontend/package.json on the host won't be reflected without a rebuild.
Minor DX nit, not blocking. Fix: mount the whole ./frontend directory
(excluding node_modules via a named volume or .dockerignore) or add the
missing files individually.
DONE-CRITERIA: editing frontend/index.html on the host and refreshing
the dev server (already running via docker compose up) shows the change
without a container rebuild.

title: backend Dockerfile doesn't copy tests/, so docker compose run backend pytest fails
description:
Found during review of sandbox-yqf.2. backend/Dockerfile only COPYs the
app/ directory, not tests/, so pytest can't run inside the built
container image (only natively, which is what the current README
documents -- so this isn't breaking anything documented today, but it's
a latent gap if someone expects `docker compose run backend pytest` to
work).
DONE-CRITERIA: `docker compose run backend pytest` (or equivalent) passes
inside the container, OR the README explicitly documents that container
test execution isn't supported and native pytest is required.

title: Basement inventory list + manual status tracking
description:
INPUT: the pipeline orchestration and Item model.

ACTION:
- Backend: `GET /items` (list, filterable by status/decision query
  params) and `PATCH /items/{id}/status` to manually transition status
  to listed | given_away | disposed (user confirms they acted on the
  app's recommendation -- no automated posting to Kleinanzeigen, per
  epic assumption/decision).
- Frontend: inventory list view showing all items with photo thumbnail,
  decision, status, and a control to advance status (e.g. "Mark as
  listed on Kleinanzeigen", "Mark as given away", "Mark as disposed"),
  plus filters by status/decision.

EDGE CASES: reject invalid status transitions (e.g. jumping straight
from pending_identification to disposed) with a 400 and a clear message
listing valid next states from the current one.

OUTPUT: endpoints + UI, committed.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- Backend tests: GET /items respects status/decision filters; PATCH
  /items/{id}/status succeeds for valid transitions and returns 400 with
  the correct message for an invalid one.
- Manual test or component test confirms the UI list renders items
  grouped/filterable by status and the status-advance controls call the
  PATCH endpoint correctly.

title: Frontend: item results view
description:
INPUT: GET /items/{id} endpoint.

ACTION: Build a results page showing: the uploaded photo, identified
name/category, the recommended decision (sell/give-away/throw-away)
rendered clearly, the suggested price (when decision=sell), and a list
of the comparable Kleinanzeigen listings with clickable links to the
original listings.
